task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: separability from talent and player counts
methodological_questions: How to measure lineup coverage from play-by-play and role classifications
How to isolate coverage effect from confounding by overall player talent
How to implement a talent control that does not introduce artifacts
Whether coverage varies sufficiently within team to yield adequate power

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality (pct_ran_BEST - pct_ran_AVOID) vs talent as predictor of series wins: corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. Per-series logistic: talent_diff_z +0.737 p=0.0213; adapt_diff_z +0.328 p=0.2755. Team-in-series cluster: talent p=0.0095, adapt p=0.2449. Univariate adapt beta=+0.311 p=0.1128. After talent control adapt p=0.275; n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate: Hypothesis that play-type actions have decaying cross-possession memory (lag-1 ≥ lag-2). FAIL decay-sanity: DRIVE lifts flat (+0.015,+0.020,...); within-team DRIVE lag-1 +0.015 to -0.002. Cohen d ~0.01-0.03; flat non-decaying lifts collapse under within-team baseline; team-quality confound.

Sequence-memory lag effects with game-state controls: Naive lag-1 PPP effects: d(1)=+0.024 AUC, d(2)=+0.004. SPOT_UP lag-1 survives controls, but DRIVE lag-1 p=0.0000 becomes ctrl_p=0.0911, PNR naive p=0.031 becomes controlled 0.136, within-team lift ~0. Lag-1 effects for DRIVE/PNR disappear with game-state controls / within-team baseline.

Execution conformance of observed mix vs recommended plan: avg |delta| on leverage buckets 4.5pp to 24.0pp; best matched opener #3 in half the sides. Single-game descriptive study, no outcome comparison.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating coaching adaptation from talent in playoff series
failed_approaches.why: Small sample (n~55 series) led to inability to distinguish adaptation from talent; talent and adaptation were correlated (+0.124), and after talent control adapt was not significant (p=0.275).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing for decaying cross-possession memory of play-type actions
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts collapsed under within-team baseline; apparent effects were driven by team-quality confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting sequence-memory lag effects with game-state controls
failed_approaches.why: DRIVE and PNR lag-1 effects disappeared when using within-team baselines or game-state controls, indicating team-quality confound rather than genuine carryover.

evidence_establishes: Within-team baselines are critical to avoid spurious effects from team-quality confounding.
Small samples (e.g., 55 series) can be insufficient to separate structural effects from talent.
Game-state controls (period, score margin, clock) can eliminate naive possession-level carryover effects.
The project has a working role classification (organizer, shaper, terminal) derived from the Structural Influence framework.
evidence_does_not_establish: The degree of within-team variation in lineup coverage (≥1 organizer, shaper, terminal).
Whether such coverage is separable from player talent and simple player counts.
How a talent control would behave when applied to a binary coverage measure.
Any direct evidence on the predictive power or practical relevance of lineup coverage.
own_inferences: With 420,993 possessions and 90 team-seasons, there is likely sufficient data to detect small effects if coverage varies meaningfully.
The main threat is low variance: many teams may almost always have all three roles on the floor, leaving few 'uncovered' stints.
Role definitions (organizer, shaper, terminal) rely on within-season usage and residual influence, which could introduce look-ahead bias if not handled carefully.

A within-team fixed-effects design, similar to the baselines used in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work], can mitigate team-level confounding but may still be affected by lineup-specific quality.
uncertainties: Actual base rate of lineups lacking at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal.
Power to detect a coverage effect of plausible size (e.g., 0.015 PPP) given unknown within-team variance.
Possible collinearity between coverage and the simple count of high-usage players.
Reliability of role assignments for players near the usage/residual thresholds.
Stability of role classifications when using only early-season data to avoid look-ahead.

historical_effect.explanation: No prior study directly tested lineup coverage; the retrieval returned no directly applicable answer. However, the historical failures strongly informed design choices, particularly the necessity of within-team fixed effects and careful handling of confounding by overall team quality.

blocking_constraints.text: If lineups without full coverage (≥1 organizer, shaper, terminal) occur in fewer than ~5% of stints, there will be insufficient variation to estimate the effect with useful power.
Some teams may never field a lineup missing one of the three roles, making within-team estimation impossible for those teams.

prior_work.summary: No earlier study examined lineup coverage. Related work on adaptation quality ([prior work][prior work]) and play-type memory ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) underscores the danger of team-quality confounding and the need for within-team baselines.

risks.text: If the proportion of stints lacking full coverage is very low, the design will be underpowered and may produce unreliable estimates.
Some team-seasons may have zero uncovered stints, reducing the effective sample and forcing between-team comparisons that confound coverage with team quality.
Even within team, uncovered stints may occur when stars are resting, conflating coverage with the absence of top talent.
Role assignments (organizer, shaper, terminal) are based on usage and residual influence thresholds; players near boundaries may be misclassified, introducing noise.
Defining roles from the same season’s data may cause regression to the mean in coverage effects if extreme role assignments are less stable.
Using full-season role labels to classify early-season stints creates a look-ahead bias; role assignments must use only prior data.
A binary coverage measure may be too coarse; a gradient (e.g., number of missing roles, or continuous structural influence sum) might be more informative but is not part of the stated question.
If investigators explore several coverage thresholds or subgroups, multiplicity must be accounted for to avoid inflated false-positive rates.

design.estimand: The effect of stint-level lineup structural coverage (binary: presence of ≥1 player in each role category — organizer, shaper, terminal) on offensive points per possession, controlling for player talent and game context.
design.unit: Stint (possession-aggregated to stint, or possession-level with stint-level coverage indicator).
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff stints from NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26, excluding garbage time (final 5 minutes with margin ≥20). Restrict to stints with ≥5 possessions to reduce noise.
design.power: Power analysis will be conducted via Monte Carlo simulation using pilot within-team variance of coverage and effect-size estimates from previous role studies (targeting Cohen’s d ≥ 0.01). Aim for >80% power to detect a 0.015 PPP difference at α=0.05.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects (within-team comparison). Player fixed effects for the five offensive players on the floor (or their aggregated prior net rating to avoid absorbing coverage). Game-state controls: period (1-4), score margin (linear and quadratic), seconds remaining in clock. Home/away indicator.
design.falsification: 1) Placebo test: randomly reassign coverage labels across stints within each team-season; the effect should be null. 2) Negative control: test coverage of the opposing defense on own offensive PPP; it should be unrelated. 3) Check that talent proxies alone (e.g., sum of offensive box plus-minus) cannot reproduce the coverage effect.
design.multiplicity: Primary hypothesis is the single coverage indicator. Any subgroup analyses (e.g., by half, by play type) will be corrected using Bonferroni-Holm and reported as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Two-tailed test at α=0.05. Pre-register a minimum of 10 stints per team-season with and without coverage; team-seasons failing this threshold are excluded but reported. If fewer than 10 teams remain, aggregate across seasons and test only the cross-team design with team random effects, but downgrade to exploratory.
design.data_version: Complete NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 seasons (regular and playoffs), as available on 2026-07-13. Role classifications will be derived from the preceding season’s data to avoid look-ahead; for 2022-23, use 2021-22 data if available, otherwise fall back to split-half within-season assignment with a holdout check.
